text: Entry Requirements 1. Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with a valid passport (according to the Nationality Law of The People's Republic of China), and the conditions set by the Document No. 12 (2020) of Ministry of Education of the PRC should be met; be in good health and get good grades. 2. Applicants must abide by the laws and regulations of the Chinese government and local government as well as the regulations of SWUFE. 3. Applicants' education background should meet one of the conditions below: (1) Nation-recognized senior high school students who will graduate in the current year must obtain a nation-recognized corresponding diploma before enrolling in the year of admission, otherwise, the admission qualification will be invalid. (2) Applicants have had a nation-recognized senior high school diploma. (3) Applicants have had a Bachelor's degree. 4. Age Limit: 18 to 35 years old. 5. Requirements for Language Proficiency A. Pass the Professional Chinese Test of China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA). B. If the Applicants who apply for the undergraduate program in Chinese Language and Literature, pass HSK Level 4 with a total score over 180 points, the Professional Chinese Test of CSCA could be waived. 6. Application Remarks A. Applicants for Chinese-taught programs must select the Chinese language version of the CSCA test and cannot choose the English language version. Applicants for English-taught programs must select the English language version of the CSCA test. B. For Chinese-medium programs, applicants must take both the "Professional Chinese" and "Mathematics" subjects. For English-taught programs, only the "Mathematics" subject is required. C. The Professional Chinese Test of CSCA is divided into two categories: Humanities Chinese and STEM Chinese. The test covers subjects corresponding to your intended major (Please check SWUFE 2026 Academic Program List, download here ). D. Applicants for undergraduate programs in Chinese Language and Literature at the School of Humanities and Arts who submit an HSK Level 4 score of 180 or above will be exempt from the Professional Chinese Test of CSCA. Notes: To ensure a smooth application process, we recommend taking the CSCA as early as possible and submitting your scores promptly to allow ample time for subsequent review. Before the CSCA exam, applicants may submit only the successful exam registration page as a reference.
